paragraphs.text: Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος· καὶ καθίσαντος αὐτοῦ προσῆλθαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Idōn de tous ochlous anebē eis to oros· kai kathisantos autou prosēlthan autō hoi mathētai autou·

i18n.en: And seeing the crowds, he went up onto the mountain; and when he had sat down, his disciples came to him.

notes.official: *anebē eis to oros* — Jesus 'went up onto the mountain'. The Matthean mountain-setting opens the structural-theological pattern of mountain-as-revelation-site that recurs at Mt 17:1 (Transfiguration) and Mt 28:16 (Great Commission). D. C. Allison, *The New Moses* (Fortress 1993), treats the Sermon-on-the-Mount mountain as Matthean Moses-typology — Jesus teaches Torah on the mountain, parallel to Moses on Sinai (Ex 19-20). See `mountain-as-revelation-site-mt-cross-corpus-har-sinai-mount-sapunu`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς λέγων·
paragraphs.translit: kai anoixas to stoma autou edidasken autous legōn·

i18n.en: And opening his mouth, he taught them, saying:

paragraphs.text: Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοὶ τῷ πνεύματι, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Makarioi hoi ptōchoi tō pneumati, hoti autōn estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn.

i18n.en: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.

notes.official: *Makarioi hoi ptōchoi tō pneumati* — the first beatitude. *makarios* (LXX-Greek standardly rendering Hebrew *ʾašrê*) opens the Hebrew wisdom-beatitude tradition (Ps 1:1; 32:1; 119:1-2). The Matthean *tō pneumati* spiritualization (vs the Lukan *ptōchoi* simple-poverty at Lk 6:20) likely reflects an Aramaic-Hebrew *ʿănāwîm* / 1QM 11:9 *ʿnwy rwḥ* 'humble-of-spirit' Qumran-community background. *basileia tōn ouranōn* — the Matthean-distinctive rabbinic-*malkhut shamayim*-style circumlocution; see `beatitudes-mt-5-3-12-makarios-formula-ethical-teaching-cross-corpus` and `kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim`.

paragraphs.text: μακάριοι οἱ πενθοῦντες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ παρακληθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi penthountes, hoti autoi paraklēthēsontai.

i18n.en: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.

notes.official: *makarioi hoi penthountes* — the mourners-beatitude. Direct LXX-citation of Isa 61:2 *parakalesai pantas tous penthountas* 'to comfort all who mourn'. The Matthean Jesus opens the SM with the Isa 61 Servant-of-YHWH program — the proclamation of liberation to the brokenhearted. Davies-Allison ICC 1.448-449.

paragraphs.text: μακάριοι οἱ πραεῖς, ὅτι αὐτοὶ κληρονομήσουσιν τὴν γῆν.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi praeis, hoti autoi klēronomēsousin tēn gēn.

i18n.en: Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.

notes.official: *makarioi hoi praeis ... klēronomēsousin tēn gēn* — direct LXX-citation of Ps 37:11 *praeis ... klēronomēsousin gēn* 'the meek shall inherit the land'. The *gē* admits both 'earth' (cosmic) and 'land' (Israelite-territorial). The Hebrew *ʾereṣ* at Ps 37:11 has both senses; the Matthean *gē* preserves the ambiguity. Davies-Allison ICC 1.449-451.

paragraphs.text: μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες καὶ διψῶντες τὴν δικαιοσύνην, ὅτι αὐτοὶ χορτασθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi peinōntes kai dipsōntes tēn dikaiosynēn, hoti autoi chortasthēsontai.

i18n.en: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.

notes.official: *peinōntes kai dipsōntes tēn dikaiosynēn* — hunger-and-thirst-for-righteousness. The wisdom-tradition hunger-for-wisdom motif (Prov 9:5; Sir 24:21; Wisdom 7:7); also echoes Isa 55:1-2 (the prophetic invitation to drink-without-cost). The Matthean *dikaiosynē* covers both forensic-righteousness and ethical-justice-doing; the philological breadth is preserved.

paragraphs.text: μακάριοι οἱ ἐλεήμονες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ ἐλεηθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi eleēmones, hoti autoi eleēthēsontai.

i18n.en: Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.

paragraphs.text: μακάριοι οἱ καθαροὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ, ὅτι αὐτοὶ τὸν θεὸν ὄψονται.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi katharoi tē kardia, hoti autoi ton theon opsontai.

i18n.en: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.

notes.official: *katharoi tē kardia ... ton theon opsontai* — pure-in-heart shall-see-God. Direct LXX-citation of Ps 24:4 *kathar tē kardia*. The promise *ton theon opsontai* sits in tension with the Ex 33:20 'no one can see God and live' tradition; the prophetic *seeing-YHWH* tradition (Isa 6:1-5; Ezek 1; Dan 7) is the cross-corpus background. The beatific-vision theological tradition derives substantially from this verse + Heb 12:14. Davies-Allison ICC 1.456-457.

paragraphs.text: μακάριοι οἱ εἰρηνοποιοί, ὅτι αὐτοὶ υἱοὶ θεοῦ κληθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi eirēnopoioi, hoti autoi huioi theou klēthēsontai.

i18n.en: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.

paragraphs.text: μακάριοι οἱ δεδιωγμένοι ἕνεκεν δικαιοσύνης, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi dediōgmenoi heneken dikaiosynēs, hoti autōn estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn.

i18n.en: Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.

notes.official: *hoi dediōgmenoi heneken dikaiosynēs ... basileia tōn ouranōn* — the eighth beatitude closes the eight-beatitude structural-pattern with the inclusio repetition of the kingdom-promise from v.3 (theirs is the kingdom of the heavens). Davies-Allison ICC 1.459-462.

paragraphs.text: μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν ὀνειδίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ διώξωσιν καὶ εἴπωσιν πᾶν πονηρὸν καθ' ὑμῶν ψευδόμενοι ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: makarioi este hotan oneidisōsin hymas kai diōxōsin kai eipōsin pan ponēron kath' hymōn pseudomenoi heneken emou·

i18n.en: Blessed are you when they revile you and persecute you and speak every kind of evil against you, lying, on my account.

notes.official: The expanded ninth beatitude (vv.11-12) shifts to direct-address (*hymeis*) and breaks the third-person pattern. Generally treated as a Matthean expansion of the original eight-beatitude unit, addressing the situation of the Matthean community under persecution. Davies-Allison ICC 1.464-467.

paragraphs.text: χαίρετε καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, ὅτι ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· οὕτως γὰρ ἐδίωξαν τοὺς προφήτας τοὺς πρὸ ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: chairete kai agalliasthe, hoti ho misthos hymōn polys en tois ouranois· houtōs gar ediōxan tous prophētas tous pro hymōn.

i18n.en: Rejoice and be glad, for your reward in the heavens is great; for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you.

paragraphs.text: Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ ἅλας τῆς γῆς· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ, ἐν τίνι ἁλισθήσεται; εἰς οὐδὲν ἰσχύει ἔτι εἰ μὴ βληθὲν ἔξω καταπατεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
paragraphs.translit: Hymeis este to halas tēs gēs· ean de to halas mōranthē, en tini halisthēsetai? eis ouden ischyei eti ei mē blēthen exō katapateisthai hypo tōn anthrōpōn.

i18n.en: You are the salt of the earth; but if the salt has lost its savor, with what shall it be salted? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trodden underfoot by people.

paragraphs.text: Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου. οὐ δύναται πόλις κρυβῆναι ἐπάνω ὄρους κειμένη·
paragraphs.translit: Hymeis este to phōs tou kosmou. ou dynatai polis krybēnai epanō orous keimenē·

i18n.en: You are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hidden.

notes.official: *hē polis ... epanō orous keimenē* — 'a city set upon a mountain'. Possible echoes: Isa 2:2-3 / Mic 4:1-2 (the eschatological-Zion drawing all nations to the mountain-of-YHWH); the Sermon-on-the-Mount mountain itself. The Matthean structural-pattern of mountain-as-revelation-site is operative. See `mountain-as-revelation-site-mt-cross-corpus-har-sinai-mount-sapunu`.

paragraphs.text: οὐδὲ καίουσιν λύχνον καὶ τιθέασιν αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, καὶ λάμπει πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: oude kaiousin lychnon kai titheasin auton hypo ton modion all' epi tēn lychnian, kai lampei pasin tois en tē oikia.

i18n.en: Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a basket, but on a lampstand, and it gives light to all who are in the house.

paragraphs.text: οὕτως λαμψάτω τὸ φῶς ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὅπως ἴδωσιν ὑμῶν τὰ καλὰ ἔργα καὶ δοξάσωσιν τὸν πατέρα ὑμῶν τὸν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs lampsatō to phōs hymōn emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn, hopōs idōsin hymōn ta kala erga kai doxasōsin ton patera hymōn ton en tois ouranois.

i18n.en: Even so, let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in the heavens.

paragraphs.text: Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον καταλῦσαι τὸν νόμον ἢ τοὺς προφήτας· οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι·
paragraphs.translit: Mē nomisēte hoti ēlthon katalysai ton nomon ē tous prophētas· ouk ēlthon katalysai alla plērōsai·

i18n.en: Do not think that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I did not come to abolish, but to fulfill.

notes.official: **The central Matthean Torah-stance statement.** *Mē nomisēte hoti ēlthon katalysai ... ouk ēlthon katalysai alla plērōsai* — 'do not think I came to abolish ... I came to fulfill'. The verb-pair *katalysai* (abolish) vs *plērōsai* (fulfill / fill-to-fullness) carries the entire weight of the Matthean Torah-stance. The Matthean Jesus explicitly disavows Torah-abrogation; the antitheses that follow (vv.21-48) are intensifications, not replacements. The Christian-supersessionist reading (Marcionite tendencies; Reformation law-vs-grace; dispensationalism) is a downstream 2nd-c.-and-later development that the Matthean text resists. See `abolish-or-fulfill-mt-5-17-katalysai-vs-plērōsai-christian-supersessionism-disavowal-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἕως ἂν παρέλθῃ ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ, ἰῶτα ἓν ἢ μία κεραία οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.
paragraphs.translit: amēn gar legō hymin, heōs an parelthē ho ouranos kai hē gē, iōta hen ē mia keraia ou mē parelthē apo tou nomou, heōs an panta genētai.

i18n.en: For amen I say to you: until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke shall pass away from the Law, until all is accomplished.

notes.official: *amēn legō hymin* — the Matthean Aramaic-loan *amēn* preserved untranslated, marking solemn-declaration. *iōta hen ē mia keraia* 'one yota or one stroke' — the smallest Hebrew letter (yod) and the smallest scribal mark (keraia). The Matthean Jesus' Torah-preservation-statement is explicit and uncompromising. Davies-Allison ICC 1.488-495.

paragraphs.text: ὃς ἐὰν οὖν λύσῃ μίαν τῶν ἐντολῶν τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων καὶ διδάξῃ οὕτως τοὺς ἀνθρώπους, ἐλάχιστος κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν· ὃς δ' ἂν ποιήσῃ καὶ διδάξῃ, οὗτος μέγας κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hos ean oun lysē mian tōn entolōn toutōn tōn elachistōn kai didaxē houtōs tous anthrōpous, elachistos klēthēsetai en tē basileia tōn ouranōn· hos d' an poiēsē kai didaxē, houtos megas klēthēsetai en tē basileia tōn ouranōn.

i18n.en: Whoever therefore relaxes one of the least of these commandments and so teaches others, shall be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does and teaches them, this one shall be called great in the kingdom of the heavens.

notes.official: The escalation-clause: those who break-and-teach-others-to-break the commandments will be *elachistos* (least) in the kingdom; those who do-and-teach-them will be *megas* (great). The Matthean Jesus reinforces Torah-observance at the highest pitch.

paragraphs.text: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ περισσεύσῃ ὑμῶν ἡ δικαιοσύνη πλεῖον τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: legō gar hymin hoti ean mē perisseusē hymōn hē dikaiosynē pleion tōn grammateōn kai Pharisaiōn, ou mē eiselthēte eis tēn basileian tōn ouranōn.

i18n.en: For I say to you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter the kingdom of the heavens.

notes.official: *ean mē perisseusē hymōn hē dikaiosynē pleion tōn grammateōn kai Pharisaiōn* — 'unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees'. The Matthean intensification: the SM-ethic exceeds Pharisaic Torah-observance, not replaces it. The polemical-edge against scribes-and-Pharisees is a Matthean redactional feature; modern Jewish-Christian dialogue (Levine 2006; JANT 2017) emphasizes that the 1st-c. polemic is intra-Jewish, not anti-Jewish, and supersessionist readings are downstream Christian-misappropriations.

paragraphs.text: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐ φονεύσεις· ὃς δ' ἂν φονεύσῃ, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει.
paragraphs.translit: Ēkousate hoti errethē tois archaiois· Ou phoneuseis· hos d' an phoneusē, enochos estai tē krisei.

i18n.en: You have heard that it was said to those of old: "You shall not murder"; and whoever murders shall be liable to judgment.

notes.official: **The first antithesis** (vv.21-26) on murder/anger. *errethē tois archaiois ... egō de legō hymin* — the antithetical-formula 'you have heard it said ... but I say to you' opens the six antitheses. The formula does NOT abrogate Torah; it intensifies-and-internalizes (anger as root of murder; lust as root of adultery). Davies-Allison ICC 1.504-510.

paragraphs.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὀργιζόμενος τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει· ὃς δ' ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ· Ῥακά, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῷ συνεδρίῳ· ὃς δ' ἂν εἴπῃ· Μωρέ, ἔνοχος ἔσται εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός.
paragraphs.translit: egō de legō hymin hoti pas ho orgizomenos tō adelphō autou enochos estai tē krisei· hos d' an eipē tō adelphō autou· Rhaka, enochos estai tō synedriō· hos d' an eipē· Mōre, enochos estai eis tēn geennan tou puros.

i18n.en: But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment; and whoever says to his brother, "Raca" (empty-head), shall be liable to the council; and whoever says, "You fool," shall be liable to the gehenna of fire.

notes.official: *rhaka* — Greek transliteration of Aramaic *reqaʾ* 'empty-headed one, fool'. Matthew preserves the Aramaic loan-word untranslated, evidencing the Aramaic-substratum of the Jesus-tradition. Three-fold judgment escalation: anger → judgment; rhaka → council; mōre → gehenna-of-fire. See overlay entry `raca-aramaic-insult-untranslated-mt-5-22`.

paragraphs.text: ἐὰν οὖν προσφέρῃς τὸ δῶρόν σου ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον κἀκεῖ μνησθῇς ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἔχει τι κατὰ σοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: ean oun prospherēs to dōron sou epi to thysiastērion kakei mnēsthēs hoti ho adelphos sou echei ti kata sou,

i18n.en: If therefore you are bringing your gift to the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,

paragraphs.text: ἄφες ἐκεῖ τὸ δῶρόν σου ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ ὕπαγε πρῶτον διαλλάγηθι τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου, καὶ τότε ἐλθὼν πρόσφερε τὸ δῶρόν σου.
paragraphs.translit: aphes ekei to dōron sou emprosthen tou thysiastēriou kai hypage prōton diallagēthi tō adelphō sou, kai tote elthōn prosphere to dōron sou.

i18n.en: leave your gift there before the altar and go: first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.

paragraphs.text: ἴσθι εὐνοῶν τῷ ἀντιδίκῳ σου ταχὺ ἕως ὅτου εἶ μετ' αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, μήποτέ σε παραδῷ ὁ ἀντίδικος τῷ κριτῇ, καὶ ὁ κριτὴς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ, καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν βληθήσῃ·
paragraphs.translit: isthi eunoōn tō antidikō sou tachy heōs hotou ei met' autou en tē hodō, mēpote se paradō ho antidikos tō kritē, kai ho kritēs tō hypēretē, kai eis phylakēn blēthēsē·

i18n.en: Make friends quickly with your accuser while you are with him on the way, lest your accuser hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.

paragraphs.text: ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως ἂν ἀποδῷς τὸν ἔσχατον κοδράντην.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō soi, ou mē exelthēs ekeithen heōs an apodōs ton eschaton kodrantēn.

i18n.en: Amen I say to you, you shall by no means come out from there until you have paid the last quadrans.

paragraphs.text: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Οὐ μοιχεύσεις.
paragraphs.translit: Ēkousate hoti errethē· Ou moicheuseis.

i18n.en: You have heard that it was said: "You shall not commit adultery."

notes.official: **The second antithesis** (vv.27-30) on adultery/lust. The intensification: not only the act but the look-with-intent (*epithymēsai autēn*) constitutes adultery. The Matthean ethics internalizes Torah at the level of intention. Davies-Allison ICC 1.521-525.

paragraphs.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ βλέπων γυναῖκα πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτὴν ἤδη ἐμοίχευσεν αὐτὴν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: egō de legō hymin hoti pas ho blepōn gynaika pros to epithymēsai autēn ēdē emoicheusen autēn en tē kardia autou.

i18n.en: But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

paragraphs.text: εἰ δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ὁ δεξιὸς σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου βληθῇ εἰς γέενναν.
paragraphs.translit: ei de ho ophthalmos sou ho dexios skandalizei se, exele auton kai bale apo sou, sympherei gar soi hina apolētai hen tōn melōn sou kai mē holon to sōma sou blēthē eis geennan.

i18n.en: If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish, than that your whole body be thrown into gehenna.

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἰ ἡ δεξιά σου χεὶρ σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔκκοψον αὐτὴν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου εἰς γέενναν ἀπέλθῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ei hē dexia sou cheir skandalizei se, ekkopson autēn kai bale apo sou, sympherei gar soi hina apolētai hen tōn melōn sou kai mē holon to sōma sou eis geennan apelthē.

i18n.en: And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish, than that your whole body go away into gehenna.

paragraphs.text: Ἐρρέθη δέ· Ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, δότω αὐτῇ ἀποστάσιον.
paragraphs.translit: Errethē de· Hos an apolysē tēn gynaika autou, dotō autē apostasion.

i18n.en: It was also said: "Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce."

notes.official: **The third antithesis** (vv.31-32) on divorce. *apolyō* + *apostasion* — the bill-of-divorcement (Deut 24:1). The Matthean exception-clause *parektos logou porneias* ('except for sexual-immorality') is a Matthean addition not in Mk 10:11 or Lk 16:18. The exception-clause is one of the most-debated Matthean Torah-redactions in the history of Christian moral-theology. Davies-Allison ICC 1.527-532.

paragraphs.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας ποιεῖ αὐτὴν μοιχευθῆναι, καὶ ὃς ἐὰν ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσῃ μοιχᾶται.
paragraphs.translit: egō de legō hymin hoti pas ho apolyōn tēn gynaika autou parektos logou porneias poiei autēn moicheuthēnai, kai hos ean apolelymenēn gamēsē moichatai.

i18n.en: But I say to you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on the ground of unchastity, causes her to commit adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

paragraphs.text: Πάλιν ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐκ ἐπιορκήσεις, ἀποδώσεις δὲ τῷ κυρίῳ τοὺς ὅρκους σου.
paragraphs.translit: Palin ēkousate hoti errethē tois archaiois· Ouk epiorkēseis, apodōseis de tō kyriō tous horkous sou.

i18n.en: Again, you have heard that it was said to those of old: "You shall not swear falsely, but shall perform to the Lord what you have sworn."

notes.official: **The fourth antithesis** (vv.33-37) on oaths. The Matthean Jesus' radical prohibition (*mē omosai holōs* 'do not swear at all') goes beyond Torah's regulation-of-oaths. Cross-corpus to Jas 5:12; Philo *Decal.* 84-95 (Hellenistic-Jewish oath-criticism); Qumran-community oath-prohibition (4Q477).

paragraphs.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ὀμόσαι ὅλως· μήτε ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὅτι θρόνος ἐστὶν τοῦ θεοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: egō de legō hymin mē omosai holōs· mēte en tō ouranō, hoti thronos estin tou theou·

i18n.en: But I say to you, do not swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God,

paragraphs.text: μήτε ἐν τῇ γῇ, ὅτι ὑποπόδιόν ἐστιν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ· μήτε εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ὅτι πόλις ἐστὶν τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως·
paragraphs.translit: mēte en tē gē, hoti hypopodion estin tōn podōn autou· mēte eis Hierosolyma, hoti polis estin tou megalou basileōs·

i18n.en: nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King;

paragraphs.text: μήτε ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ σου ὀμόσῃς, ὅτι οὐ δύνασαι μίαν τρίχα λευκὴν ποιῆσαι ἢ μέλαιναν.
paragraphs.translit: mēte en tē kephalē sou omosēs, hoti ou dynasai mian tricha leukēn poiēsai ē melainan.

i18n.en: nor shall you swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black.

paragraphs.text: ἔστω δὲ ὁ λόγος ὑμῶν ναὶ ναί, οὒ οὔ· τὸ δὲ περισσὸν τούτων ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: estō de ho logos hymōn nai nai, ou ou· to de perisson toutōn ek tou ponērou estin.

i18n.en: But let your word be "Yes, yes," "No, no"; anything beyond these is from the evil one.

paragraphs.text: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ὀφθαλμὸν ἀντὶ ὀφθαλμοῦ καὶ ὀδόντα ἀντὶ ὀδόντος.
paragraphs.translit: Ēkousate hoti errethē· Ophthalmon anti ophthalmou kai odonta anti odontos.

i18n.en: You have heard that it was said: "An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth."

notes.official: **The fifth antithesis** (vv.38-42) on retaliation. *Ophthalmon anti ophthalmou* — the lex talionis (Ex 21:24; Lev 24:20; Deut 19:21). The Matthean Jesus' non-retaliation teaching does not abrogate Torah's judicial-principle but transforms-it for inter-personal ethics. Davies-Allison ICC 1.540-548.

paragraphs.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ἀντιστῆναι τῷ πονηρῷ· ἀλλ' ὅστις σε ῥαπίζει εἰς τὴν δεξιὰν σιαγόνα, στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην·
paragraphs.translit: egō de legō hymin mē antistēnai tō ponērō· all' hostis se rhapizei eis tēn dexian siagona, strepson autō kai tēn allēn·

i18n.en: But I say to you, do not resist the evildoer; but whoever strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.

paragraphs.text: καὶ τῷ θέλοντί σοι κριθῆναι καὶ τὸν χιτῶνά σου λαβεῖν, ἄφες αὐτῷ καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον·
paragraphs.translit: kai tō thelonti soi krithēnai kai ton chitōna sou labein, aphes autō kai to himation·

i18n.en: And to the one who wishes to sue you and take your tunic, hand over your cloak also.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὅστις σε ἀγγαρεύσει μίλιον ἕν, ὕπαγε μετ' αὐτοῦ δύο.
paragraphs.translit: kai hostis se angareusei milion hen, hypage met' autou dyo.

i18n.en: And whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.

paragraphs.text: τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δός, καὶ τὸν θέλοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ δανίσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῇς.
paragraphs.translit: tō aitounti se dos, kai ton thelonta apo sou danisasthai mē apostraphēs.

i18n.en: Give to the one who asks of you, and do not turn away from the one who wishes to borrow from you.

paragraphs.text: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου καὶ μισήσεις τὸν ἐχθρόν σου.
paragraphs.translit: Ēkousate hoti errethē· Agapēseis ton plēsion sou kai misēseis ton echthron sou.

i18n.en: You have heard that it was said: "You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy."

notes.official: **The sixth antithesis** (vv.43-48) on enemy-love. *agapēseis ton plēsion sou* — Lev 19:18 LXX. The *miseseis ton echthron sou* 'you shall hate your enemy' is NOT a Torah citation; it appears at Qumran (1QS 1:10 *li-snoʾ kol benei ḥošek* 'to hate all the sons of darkness'), suggesting the Matthean Jesus engages a Qumran-sectarian rather than mainstream-rabbinic position. Davies-Allison ICC 1.549-553.

paragraphs.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν διωκόντων ὑμᾶς·
paragraphs.translit: egō de legō hymin, agapate tous echthrous hymōn kai proseuchesthe hyper tōn diōkontōn hymas·

i18n.en: But I say to you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,

paragraphs.text: ὅπως γένησθε υἱοὶ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς, ὅτι τὸν ἥλιον αὐτοῦ ἀνατέλλει ἐπὶ πονηροὺς καὶ ἀγαθοὺς καὶ βρέχει ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ἀδίκους.
paragraphs.translit: hopōs genēsthe huioi tou patros hymōn tou en ouranois, hoti ton hēlion autou anatellei epi ponērous kai agathous kai brechei epi dikaious kai adikous.

i18n.en: so that you may be sons of your Father who is in the heavens, for he makes his sun rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.

paragraphs.text: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀγαπήσητε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, τίνα μισθὸν ἔχετε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ τελῶναι τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν;
paragraphs.translit: ean gar agapēsēte tous agapōntas hymas, tina misthon echete? ouchi kai hoi telōnai to auto poiousin?

i18n.en: For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐὰν ἀσπάσησθε τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὑμῶν μόνον, τί περισσὸν ποιεῖτε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ ἐθνικοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν;
paragraphs.translit: kai ean aspasēsthe tous adelphous hymōn monon, ti perisson poieite? ouchi kai hoi ethnikoi to auto poiousin?

i18n.en: And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?

paragraphs.text: Ἔσεσθε οὖν ὑμεῖς τέλειοι ὡς ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τέλειός ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: Esesthe oun hymeis teleioi hōs ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios teleios estin.

i18n.en: You therefore shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

notes.official: *esesthe oun hymeis teleioi hōs ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios teleios estin* — 'be perfect as your heavenly Father is perfect'. The Matthean *teleios* echoes Lev 19:2 *qĕdōšîm tihyû kī qādôš ʾanî YHWH ʾĕlōhêkem* 'be holy for I YHWH your God am holy' (the Holiness Code parallel) — *teleios* in NT-Greek functionally renders Hebrew *tāmîm* 'whole, blameless, complete'. The closing-statement of the antitheses-section frames the entire SM-ethic as a holiness-imitation. Davies-Allison ICC 1.560-563.

Each question folded into a glossary entry (central or overlay) or into per-verse commentary documenting the philological, textual-critical, and cross-corpus considerations; defaults were preserved per the standard ASV/RSV scholarly-translation baseline. See per-paragraph `commentary` fields and the central glossary entries listed in `glossaryRefs[]` for full philological treatment.
